schema.title: CreateCredentialRequest
schema.description:
Every field is optional. Posting an empty body creates a working credential with a generated
name, a generated password and no file access — which is safe, but not useful until you set
`Permission`.

UserName.description:
The name used to log in. Generated for you when omitted.

Two ways it can be refused, and they differ: a name that is already in use returns `422`,
while a reserved name — `admin`, `root`, `support` and similar — is rejected by validation
with `400`. The username-availability endpoint reports both as taken, so check there first if
the name matters to you.

Alias.description: A label for humans, shown in the dashboard. Defaults to the login name.

Permission.description:
What this credential may do with files. Defaults to `none`, meaning it can connect but read
nothing — set this unless you intend exactly that.

Password.description:
A password of your choosing. Omit it and we generate one that satisfies your organization's
password policy, which is the better option — a password that fails the policy is rejected
with `400`.

HomeDirectory.description:
Where the credential lands after connecting. Defaults to `/home/{UserName}`. Must start with
a forward slash and must not end with one; it is created if it does not exist.

ChrootDirectory.description:
The highest directory this credential can reach. Defaults to `/`. Set it to the home
directory to confine the credential to its own folder.

Email.description:
Where portal invitations and password resets are sent. Leave it out for machine-to-machine
credentials.

State.description:
Set to `inactive` to create the credential without enabling it. Anything else is treated as
`active`.

ExpiresAt.description:
When access should stop working, in Unix epoch milliseconds. Must be at least a day away and
no more than a year away. Omit for a credential that does not expire.

typical.summary: A named credential for a specific system

dropbox.summary: A write-only drop box that expires
